styles.Sulafat: Read this as a warm, reassuring presenter speaking to busy parents. Natural, clear, steady pace, no long pauses:

lines.text: Three P.M. You're at work. Is the TV at home still on? And where is your child right now?
This is Maya — a family-centred A-I-o-T ecosystem for smarter and safer home management. One smart socket, one AI assistant, one family app.

Malaysian women's workforce participation just hit a record fifty-six point six percent. In our survey of seventy-three working parents, eighty percent said their children spend two hours or more a day unsupervised.
Parents juggle separate apps — seventy percent feel app fatigue — while devices on standby quietly waste almost ten percent of home electricity.

Today's options fall short. Most smart plugs handle a single socket. Voice assistants follow commands, but aren't linked to your child's screen time or location. And parental apps rarely connect to the home.
Maya connects all three — home, parent and child — in one family-centred hub that can act on context.
An E-S-P thirty-two, three-channel smart extension switches each outlet independently. Set it up over Bluetooth once, and it stays synced with every family phone in real time.
Here it is on the real hardware — one spoken command, one outlet.
That was Maya's own voice assistant. The child app adds the other half: screen time, last known location, and the outlet permissions parents set.
One app instead of many. Hands-free control. Peace of mind at work. Less wasted power — and no rewiring.
Maya delivers on four S-D-Gs: safer communities, well-being, clean energy, responsible consumption.
And on all three E-S-G pillars: less standby waste, safer children, open and secure governance.
The market is ready. Smart homes are heading to four hundred and fifty billion US dollars by twenty thirty-two, smart plugs to thirty billion, and parental-control software to over four billion.

If we take this to market, the natural buyers would be working families with school-age children. Our suggestion is a kit — the three-channel socket with the app included — at around one hundred and ninety-nine ringgit, sold through online marketplaces and school and community partners, with an optional cloud plan at ten ringgit a month, or a hundred ringgit a year.

Eighty-four percent of parents find smart extensions useful, and eighty-two percent would install a child monitoring app. Our prototype passed all forty tests on about ninety-five ringgit of hardware — and development is active: iteration four, for sensors and hubs, is underway.
Maya is open source under the Apache two point zero license, built on research at Universiti Selangor.
Other smart homes switch things on and off.
Maya understands your family.
Affordable, intelligent and open — so every working parent can breathe easy, knowing home is in good hands.
Maya: home, handled.
